Hold pending authoritative child-appropriate electrical-safety review; a broad water/appliance warning is plausible but this packet does not establish all implied actions as safe.
Hold pending Cebuano lexical verification of the alignment wording; eclipse geometry is not enough to approve a potentially changed translated relation.
Hold pending qualification of fossil evidence versus the stronger proving wording and confirmation of the exact plate-tectonics placement.
Hold pending primary NASA verification of the Webb/Hubble comparison; older/farther visibility depends on wavelength, sensitivity and target, not just launch date.
Hold pending tidal-timing scope; about an hour later each day is an approximation and must be checked against the claimed type of tide and local setting.
Hold pending PAGASA support for the stated June–October typhoon/wet-season bounds; do not infer a universal Philippine seasonal rule.
Hold pending Cebuano title verification for mountain formation and source support for the geological mechanism/scale.
Hold the unqualified stronger-water-than-wind and always-downhill comparison; force/energy depends on conditions, and fluid motion cannot be classified this way universally.
Hold pending regional scope for the Balatik/Orion naming and primary astronomical confirmation of the stated stellar color-temperature comparison.
Hold the implication that ozone protection keeps skin from burning; ozone absorbs much UV but does not guarantee freedom from sunburn.
Hold pending TL fidelity review: aquifer replenishment is expressed as pagbabago/change rather than clearly retaining recharge. Also verify the broad recharge-time range.
Hold pending density/buoyancy wording review: lightness alone does not establish flotation. Pumice porosity and water saturation require scoped explanation.
Hold the implication that a vertical air-pressure difference itself straightforwardly creates wind; hydrostatic balance and horizontal pressure gradients need distinguishing.
Hold the categorical claim that high humidity stops sweat evaporation. The effect is reduced evaporation under specified conditions, not a universal halt.
Hold pending Cebuano verification of birahay for the gravity/freefall relation and exact release/air-resistance conditions.

The gentle capture, observation and release activity would fit both proposed lessons, and all emphasis spans match. Hold the TL title: Pukot ng Insekto uses a word documented as a large/deep-sea fishing net, whereas its own body says lambat-panghuli. Need lexical/native confirmation before admitting this current title; BIS use of pukot is not the objection.

The three bodies explain visual QR encoding coherently, but never identify light as the transmission medium or communication between people. The proposed movement/sound/light lesson would require inference from camera use. BIS title also introduces Tagalog parisukat where the body uses kwadrado; no title repair authorized. No explicit supported lesson placement.

The English explicitly labels pH 6 to 7 neutral, conflating mildly acidic soil with neutral pH; TL/BIS retain the overgeneralization while dropping the numerical range. The casual just add lime also omits crop-specific testing. UMN identifies pH 7 as neutral and explains crop-dependent lime targets. Titles are aligned but scientifically faulty body is not admissible.

The approximate 3 seconds per kilometre calculation is sound and could support speed/distance-time; all emphasis spans match. Hold the current BIS body because sound naglakaw uses the walking verb in an inanimate propagation statement, a documented contextual defect in this repository and consistent with dictionary lakaw. The sound lesson would also receive only travel-rate context, not vibration production.

Retain HOLD pending authority for mainit in the current BIS title Cocoon sa Mainit nga Tubig. The hot-water silk account is plausible and the bodies retain its meaning. Later dictionary checks resolve hilo as an attested thread sense; hilo is no longer a reason for this hold. No title repair or placement is approved.

The English/TL bodies state a reasonable consequence of hearing loss, but do not name loud sound or any concrete protective measure. The historical rationale invents excessive sound exposure absent from current copy. BIS title Pagkawala sa Pamati is also lexically ambiguous against the body pandungog and corpus senses/feelings usage; hold pending lexical confirmation, not a claim that pamati is always wrong.

Thin light wings do not establish the English claim that insect flight takes very little effort: flapping flight has high metabolic costs. TL/BIS soften this into easy flight and BIS title is a further uncertain Tagalog-form rendering. The wing/function association is relevant, but this causal overstatement blocks both proposed placements. Primary insect energetics research describes high energy demands.

The oxygen/clean-water requirement is useful science for both proposed lessons, with aligned English/TL and emphasis. Hold BIS habitat: hipon sa punoan places shrimp in a trunk/main stem rather than an aquaculture pond; local corpus overwhelmingly uses punoan for tree stems or main. This changes the scenario taught. BIS title also merely repeats TL Alagang Hipon. Need current-copy language resolution first.

The English/TL distance-in-a-fixed-time comparison is useful speed science. Hold BIS: gibaktas renders a general object travelling as a distance walked/hiked, and the title Bilis needs lexical confirmation rather than assuming the Tagalog word transfers. Local corpus has only this gibaktas body; dictionary evidence for baktas is walking/hiking. All current copy was read; no edit authorized.

Read all three bodies, titles and emphasis: the beetle/Milky Way narrative is coherent, although translations omit rolling dung balls. The only proposed competency concerns how sky objects affect activities of people. An animal navigation story does not explicitly teach that scope; historical review substituted living things for people. Hold on exact lesson fit regardless of the interesting biology.

All three copies preserve boots and covering cuts, but the English so bacteria cannot get in overpromises protection and TL/BIS likewise imply prevention without qualification. For Grade 4 the current card also directs necessary flood wading without first telling children to avoid floodwater/adult help. CDC prioritizes avoiding exposure, especially with open wounds; boots and waterproof dressings reduce risk rather than guarantee safety. Hold current safety wording.

The English palm-leaf flexibility explanation would directly support bending; BIS preserves weaving/bending and emphasis is intact. Hold TL opening Malalahi ang palaspas: it does not transparently preserve can be woven and needs lexical/native verification before admission. Independently, do not infer stretching from bending for g3:solid-properties; flexibility without breakage is not evidence of stretchability.

All three bodies correctly give roots absorption and anchoring, and BIS title matches. Hold the TL title Ugat na Sumasandal ng Halaman: the leaning construction appears to reverse/lose the English support relation. This is a current title-to-body meaning uncertainty requiring lexical/native resolution, not permission to rewrite; therefore neither proposed plant lesson is admitted.

Current titles, complete bodies and emphasis consistently define carbon sequestration and name forests/oceans. The only proposed Grade 3 lesson concerns familiar local examples of science. This technical global carbon-storage definition supplies neither a concrete local activity/object nor an observable everyday science example; a general environmental category match is insufficient.

The vitamin D/calcium relation is correct and all three copies align, but all titles/bodies promote a fixed fifteen minutes of morning sun as sufficient helpful exposure without context. NIH explains that synthesis varies with time, season, skin and exposure and specifically cautions that an unqualified 15-minute rule is not meaningful. Hold this prescriptive health simplification for children.

The copy turns acoustic water recognition into proof of a clear/clean drink: BIS explicitly says limpyo and mainom, which echoes cannot establish. Smooth surfaces act as acoustic mirrors; primary experiments show bats even try drinking from smooth solid plates. The straight-back summary is incomplete and TL pumapalag is also uncertain. Both proposed sound placements are held because the current science/translation teaches an invalid cleanliness inference.

English/TL identify flammability and physiological eye/lung irritation, with matching titles/emphasis. Hold BIS makapalagot in this medical-irritation context: it is an unresolved anger/annoyance versus tissue-irritation rendering and cannot be assumed accurate. The unspecified aerosol product also makes a universal flammability statement uncertain; current copy needs specific source/lexical resolution before admission.

All three copies and emphasis retain the 4S list, but omit the essential restriction on support spraying. DOH specifies fogging/spraying only in hotspot areas with increasing dengue cases; the current unconditional line could teach indiscriminate spraying as general prevention. Hold the current health guidance despite a plausible community-solutions connection.

The emphatic cannot support plant growth claim is false as a universal in every language. Contaminated soils can support plants; EPA uses living plants for phytoremediation. Harmful contamination can impair growth, but that qualified claim is not the emphatic current copy. Titles are aligned; environmental relevance does not rescue false science.

English/TL describe soft-object deformation and would fit properties; emphasis is intact. BIS body and title render yielding as mupiyong. The local corpus uses piyong for closed eyes and the consulted Cebuano dictionary agrees, so this is a substantive changed action rather than mere style. No proposed placement is admitted with this current mistranslation.

All current bodies, titles and emphasis coherently say carbon can be stored in limestone over long periods. The proposed Grade 3 lesson is about observing/identifying nearby Earth materials and human-made objects made from them. The card supplies only hidden long-term carbon storage, with no observable material characteristic or use; rocks as a category is insufficient explicit fit.

Bodies correctly describe lighthouse light patterns carrying location information and would support community use of light; emphasis matches. Hold TL title Senaryo ng Lighthouse: scenario is not a translation of location signals and drops the teaching object identified by the English/BIS titles. Current title needs language resolution before this placement can be admitted.

Wind as moving air and the pressure-gradient tendency are useful, but English always flows from high to low pressure is an unqualified universal. NOAA explains geostrophic wind can run parallel to isobars under Coriolis balance. TL/BIS omit always yet retain the simplified one-direction rule. Current English needs qualification before the pressure/wind example is admitted.

Current titles and emphasis match, but all bodies universally say every habitat gives its organisms food sources to eat and a shelter for hiding/resting/raising young. That wording silently treats all organisms as animals; green plants make food and do not eat habitat food sources or use shelters in that way. A narrowed animal-needs statement could fit, but current universal organism scope is held.

The broad westward sunset idea is suitable locally, but current TL title Arag Lubog sa Kanluran contains Arag in place of the Sun named as araw in its own body. This is an unresolved title corruption; BIS title/body and English were also read. Always/every day additionally lacks polar-location qualification, so no current-copy admission.

A two-mirror periscope is a coherent light-reflection device, but the only proposed lesson is sending information between people; observing over an obstacle is not messaging. TL also says see sa loob ng submarino whereas English says outside a submarine and BIS from inside: the view direction is changed. Matching emphasis cannot cure either scope or translation defect.

All three bodies and emphasis align, including BIS code-switching, but the causal claim attributes Bicol-region abaca success to soil rich in ash specifically from Mayon. That broad regional attribution is not established by current card evidence; Bicol has multiple islands and volcanic/soil histories. Hold pending primary agricultural evidence for this specific causal/geographic claim, not merely the familiar volcanic-soil category.

The three bodies/titles and emphasis align on crickets eating plants plus unspecified other food. For a lesson specifically distinguishing herbivores, carnivores and omnivores, unspecified many kinds of food does not establish the animal-food part of an omnivorous diet or a defensible class. Hold this vague dietary fragment rather than silently supplying insect/prey foods from outside the card.

Bodies accurately identify a stopwatch as a seconds/timing instrument, though speed also needs distance. Both TL and BIS titles instead say Segundero; consulted dictionaries establish a seconds hand for the Spanish source word, not a stopwatch, and a target-language stopwatch sense has not been verified. Hold this current instrument-title ambiguity rather than guessing a cognate is equivalent.

Read all three complete bodies/titles: they consistently discuss dim-light eyestrain and rest, a familiar health claim. The only proposed lesson focuses on harmful bright light and loud sound; the card teaches neither bright-light hazard nor its protection. Hold on precise lesson scope rather than treating any eye-health card as sufficient.

The bodies use food or energy correctly for plants, but universally state living things breathe; that is not equivalent to all life obtaining energy, especially anaerobic organisms. Rocks/water also respond physically to environmental change, so do not do any of these is an unsafe literal boundary without biological qualification. BIS further reduces reproduce to make something new. Titles align, but the diagnostic definition is too absolute for either proposed lesson.

All three bodies, titles and emphasis align on young/lighter sailfins being better water runners. Primary zoo/breeding sources consulted establish surface running and juvenile flattened toes, but did not establish this precise juvenile-versus-adult performance and body-weight causal comparison. Because that comparison is the proposed movement-factor teaching claim, hold pending direct evidence rather than borrowing basilisk biomechanics.

All three bodies, titles and emphasis correctly name tension/stretch and compression/squeeze but assert a generic coil spring is flexible both ways. Coil springs include tightly wound extension springs and separate compression designs; a close-wound extension spring is not freely compressible from rest. Lee Spring distinguishes these designs. Hold the unqualified both-ways claim rather than teaching it as universal rigid/soft or shape-change behavior.

English correctly links windsock orientation/extension to wind, but TL/BIS titles call it Pala ng/sa Hangin, a shovel-like label unsupported for a fabric windsock; local TL corpus attests pala as shovel. TL napupulpol also does not preserve blowing direction transparently. Hold the current translation, not the valid English weather-tool concept; both proposed lessons remain blocked.

The push/pull definition and motion changes are useful and all languages/titles/emphasis align. The final claim says a heavier object simply needs stronger force to move without equal acceleration, comparable friction or other conditions; mass alone does not create such a motion threshold. This unqualified teaching claim blocks all three proposed placements despite their otherwise direct force relevance.

All three bodies, titles and emphasis convey the Pateros duck/balut reputation. The sole proposed lesson is everyday science, but the current copy is place/industry trivia with no scientific process, observation, material property or technology explanation. Hold exact fit rather than infer incubation or animal-care science that is absent.

Sunlight powering rice photosynthesis is correct, but current TL says mamulaklak ng butil, changing grow grains into an unclear flowering-of-grains action. BIS motubo og mga bugas also needs contextual confirmation because the dictionary includes milled rice as well as grain. Titles are uneven but read. Hold translation fidelity; do not silently replace these crop-development terms.

All current copies preserve the explanation, but it says iron is used in the magnets because iron is attracted, rather than explaining the iron-containing steel door. This muddles the causal answer to the fridge question. The only proposed lesson is effects without touching, while every example describes sticking/contact and never specifies action at a distance. Hold science explanation and scope.

Titles, bodies and emphasis align on lime for betel chewing from heated shells/coral. This is unsuitable standalone supplemental reading for Grade 4: it presents a carcinogenic chewing practice and caustic-lime source as an ordinary useful-material example with no age/safety framing. It also does not distinguish calcined quicklime from slaked chewing lime. IARC establishes betel-quid oral-cancer risk; neither proposed chemistry placement is admitted.

All three copies preserve the cacao-pod reuse claim and composting is plausible. The unqualified animal-feed option is not cleared for a safe-materials lesson: primary research documents variably toxic theobromine in cocoa pod husks and processing/detheobromination constraints. Current copy omits animal/species and processing limits, so both reuse/community placements are held rather than inviting indiscriminate feeding.

The bodies all discuss metres for length/distance, but current BIS title Metro sa Giladmon instead says depth. Depth is a measurable length, yet this is an unverified narrowing/substitution of the English title and its own body gitas-on/gilay-on. Also the perfect-unit wording is imprecise across measurement scales. Hold the current title fidelity rather than repairing it.

Retain HOLD for the truncated or substituted BIS title Law nga Balloon, which fails to name the spider subject present as lawalawa in the full body. Later dictionaries attest hilo for thread, so that word is not a blocker. Full trilingual bodies and titles were checked; no placement is approved.

The stridulation definition is broadly right, but English gives crickets rubbing their legs as its example. Crickets typically stridulate by rubbing their forewings; Smithsonian explicitly describes that mechanism. TL/BIS omit the incorrect example, creating a cross-language claim mismatch rather than fixing English. Hold false current science even though sound production fits the lesson.

English/TL broadly state that unspecified wave properties are used in four devices; they never identify light or sound or explain any specific energy use. BIS kabtangan also needs lexical confirmation for physical properties versus possessions; local corpus contains both senses. Hold the vague current claim rather than supply each device mechanism and wave type for the energy-uses lesson.

English correctly qualifies high-pressure weather as usually fair with little rain. TL/BIS strengthen little rain to none, and BIS title Taas nga Pressure sa Hinlo refers ambiguously to cleanness rather than clear skies; the first word Unhong also needs verification against the intended question. Hold current translation fidelity rather than infer the intended weather wording.

English/TL correctly describe meerkat underground burrows for sleep/safety, but BIS body substitutes lungib. Local corpus mixes burrow and cave uses; Wolff specifically glosses lungib as cave/hole in a slope, so the animal-dug burrow sense is not independently cleared. Hold this lexical ambiguity for native resolution, not a claim that every use of lungib is wrong.

The three titles/bodies preserve Barnard and 1967; UCT confirms the first human-to-human transplant. The supplied scientist/invention lesson requires identifying an invention, while current copy only reports who first performed a medical operation. Do not silently convert first performance into invention or credit Barnard with inventing transplantation. Hold on exact proposed lesson fit.

All current titles and emphasis were read. EN/TL sound transmission through a solid string fits the subjects, but BIS molakaw describes sound as walking and gahi changes solid-state string to hard/rigid string. These documented contextual lexical problems alter the physics description. Neither sound-transfer nor messaging placement is admitted before copy resolution.

Well-drained soil is appropriate for ube, and all three versions preserve that idea, but the further claim that Philippine volcanic and alluvial soils are therefore ideal/perfect is unsupported: geological origin does not establish drainage and texture. The DA guide separately requires good drainage and prefers organic-rich clay loam while allowing other soils. This is not cleared as an accurate example for investigating soil and plant growth. Emphasis matches, but the shared scientific overgeneralization blocks placement.

The title and all three bodies discuss living microbes, but the explanation treats eating and moving as shared diagnostic behavior of unspecified pond microbes. Photosynthetic and nonmotile microbes are included in this category: OpenStax explicitly describes autotrophic algae and nonmotile Chlorella. The card needs a named organism or narrower wording before it can support either living/nonliving comparison or signs of life; reproduction alone does not rescue the overgeneralized explanation. Emphasis is present in all bodies.

All three versions preserve the claim that a hummingbird is tiny because a bigger bird would be too heavy to hover easily. Body mass matters, but the card presents an unsupported size-only evolutionary/mechanical explanation without wing size, wing motion, or muscle capacity. Primary hummingbird work documents compensating wing allometry and strong hovering performance across body sizes. This is too imprecise for the proposed movement-factors lesson; the uncertain hover/float rendering is not used as an independent lexical defect.

The English specifically describes a mosquito pupa needing aquatic habitat, but both translated bodies drop mosquito and state the water requirement for an unspecified pupa. Terrestrial insect pupae do not require a pool of water; the missing animal qualifier therefore broadens the biological claim materially. Titles and water emphasis do not restore it. Hold both basic-needs and water-for-life placements until the current trilingual copy identifies the same organism.

All three bodies give the useful distance-divided-by-time calculation, but the BIS title Bilis sa Distansya loses the time relationship and uses a speed term whose Cebu Cebuano status remains unresolved. Corpus has 32 body uses of bilis as speed, many in a cluster with other Tagalog wording; dictionary lookup did not settle this usage. This is an uncertain title/lexical decision, not a declaration that a rare form is ungrammatical. Hold pending authoritative language clarification rather than treating the correct formula alone as a complete trilingual clearance.

The space-weather effects on satellites, radio, and electric power are scientifically supported by NOAA; the radio example added in TL/BIS remains accurate, and the titles identify the same topic. Reject the sole proposed sky-and-our-day placement: there is no daytime/nighttime observation or explanation of how ordinary sky conditions guide children’s activities. A solar-storm monitoring analogy is not evidence for this specific lesson.

All three bodies turn harder pushing into an unconditional faster-or-farther result, ending with another speed-up assertion. A push opposing existing motion can slow or stop an object, and speed/distance comparisons also require a fixed object and comparable push duration and conditions. The current wording therefore risks teaching force as always producing faster movement. Titles and emphasis translate consistently, but hold both moving-things and change-motion placements for the shared scientific ambiguity.

The three bodies accurately describe roots growing toward moisture as hydrotropism, directly relevant to growth/response. The TL and BIS titles instead read as roots growing in water, dropping the directional relationship that the English title teaches. This unresolved title meaning should be checked before admitting the full trilingual card. For plant-parts, the body also does not explicitly explain water uptake or anchoring; do not infer a root job from growth direction alone.

The artificial iron-plus-nonmagnetic-sand demonstration is useful, and the translations preserve it, but current English promises that a magnet leaves all sand behind without specifying nonmagnetic sand. Sand can include magnetite grains: NPS supplies an elementary activity specifically extracting magnetic grains from sand. A materials-investigation reading should not teach all sand as nonmagnetic. Titles/emphasis otherwise match; hold for the unqualified material claim.

EN says water cannot pass through clay and concludes some places have no groundwater for that reason. Clay has low permeability, not universally zero permeability, and groundwater occurrence also depends on recharge and subsurface structure. USGS distinguishes porosity from connected flow and says clay restricts flow. TL/BIS soften both absolutes to difficult passage and differing amounts, so they do not preserve the English claim either. This card cannot provide a consistent accurate soil comparison as written; emphasis itself matches.

Dry cogon flammability and rapid post-fire regrowth are scientifically supported, and TL/BIS retain both facts. However, English adds do not worry as reassurance about a grass fire because the grass returns. In a Grade 4 burning-properties context that minimizes a real fire hazard; the Forest Service identifies cogongrass as producing severe fire hazards. Hold for age/safety framing, not because regrowth or the translations are false. Emphasis matches.

All three versions accurately describe an existing practice of feeding kitchen leftovers to pigs, but this is not an acceptable positive example of safe reuse/disposal. Unqualified food-scrap feeding can transmit African swine fever; the Philippine DA/ATI prevention material explicitly advises avoiding swill feeding. The current card supplies no restriction or disease context, so the proposed safe-materials placement would imply safety not established by the text. Titles/emphasis otherwise preserve the meaning.

Drying and weaving water-hyacinth stalks into goods is supported by DOST and would directly support useful changes. Wolff attests habul as weaving, so the BIS weaving word is not rejected merely because Binisaya also lists blanket. The remaining BIS punoan for the harvested stalks is unresolved: corpus uses include trunk, main plant stem, and stalk, while dictionary results did not establish the needed leaf-stalk sense for water hyacinth. Because the material part being processed is central to the example, hold this lexical decision for authoritative clarification. EN/TL and all emphasis are otherwise coherent.

Muscles pulling bones to produce the listed skeletal movements is sound introductory biology, and the three titles preserve that relationship. The BIS body changes English wave / TL makakaway to makakumo. Binisaya identifies kumo as fist and kinumo as clenched fist; clenching a fist is a different action from waving. Although both involve muscles, this is a current translation substitution, not a register preference. Hold the complete trilingual body-systems card pending correction; there are no emphasis spans.

The bodies preserve the useful forked-tongue scent-direction explanation, supported by Smithsonian’s account of paired tongue-tip sampling. The current titles are not cleared: TL Dilang Sawang uses a word whose consulted dictionary senses are gap/depression rather than an established forked-tongue description, and BIS Dila nga may duha ends at with two without naming tips or branches. Corpus did not establish sawang as this anatomical adjective. Hold for ambiguous/incomplete translated titles rather than guessing a repair; TL emphasis itself matches.

Heating can inactivate germs, but all three versions turn cooking and boiling water of uncertain cleanliness into an unqualified guarantee of safe eating/drinking. Boiling does not make chemically contaminated water safe; CDC explicitly excludes fuel, toxic chemicals, and radioactive contaminants. The food claim also omits adequate heating conditions. Because this is practical child-facing safety guidance, the current blanket assurance is too broad even as an energy-causes-change example. Titles are coherent and there are no emphasis spans.

All three bodies assert that scissors handles are longer than their blades and therefore always amplify force. Scissors vary; mechanical advantage depends on distances from pivot to applied force and cutting point. Titles and matching emphasis reinforce that unsupported universal premise. Neither proposed lever lesson should use this copy.

TL/BIS faithfully reproduce the English claim, with matching Balatik emphasis, but the claim equates Balatik specifically with Orion's Belt and broadly attributes it to early Filipinos. The National Museum identifies Balatik with Orion and distinguishes ethnolinguistic sky traditions; this does not establish the narrower belt identification or this planting/harvesting claim for the unspecified community. Hold both sky-navigation and community-sky-knowledge pending attributed cultural evidence.

All three languages and emphasis repeat the misleading claim that Taal is among the smallest active volcanoes. Smithsonian distinguishes the 5-km Volcano Island from the much larger 15-by-20-km Taal caldera. Community proximity is useful risk context, but that cannot rescue the central size misconception for local-volcano-risk.

The hand-out-of-a-moving-car example invites an unsafe activity for grade-school readers. Lift direction also depends on the direction of tilt, which none of the languages specifies. TL/BIS preserve the unsafe setup; titles and emphasis do not resolve it. Hold the contact-forces placement.

English correctly restricts the changing illuminated area to the part facing us. TL and BIS omit that viewing qualification and state that the size of the illuminated part changes, which can teach the wrong mechanism for phases. Reflection and titles are otherwise usable and spans match, but the omitted distinction is central to moon-phases.

Ovary location and role fit human-reproduction and EN/TL are usable, but BIS uses porma-ovo for oval-shaped. Current corpus attestation found only three closely related ovary cards, not independent evidence that this is comprehensible Cebuano. Hold the unresolved lexical rendering for a native/dictionary decision; do not infer correctness from repeated generated wording. No emphasis is specified.

The sulfur-and-heat account of vulcanization is broadly sound and both translations preserve strengthening rubber, with consistent titles. However, the text never identifies a chemical change, new chemical structure, or a physical-versus-chemical distinction. Strength after heating alone is insufficient evidence for the proposed physical-chemical lesson's defining concept. No emphasis is specified.

The construction is incomplete for child use: unspecified wire directly across a battery can short and heat rapidly, and bare turns on a nail are not the required insulated coil. All three languages give the same unrestricted build instruction; titles and emphasis do not add insulation, disconnection or adult guidance. Hold the electromagnets construction placement.

The contamination/fair-test science and TL copy are sound, but BIS changes keep tools clean to Panalipdi ang limpyo nga gamit, i.e. protect the clean equipment. Independent corpus uses of panalipdi concern protecting habitat/eagles, not maintaining cleanliness. The later rinse instruction is useful but does not repair the opening mistranslation. Titles are consistent and no spans are specified.

The galena description is a mineral/ore fact, not an observation of a rock or a comparison of rocks. TL/BIS preserve the shiny grey cubic-crystal and weight claims; titles and spans match. The proposed rock-observation placement would rely on a loose mineral-to-rock association absent from the body.

All languages assert a ranked material comparison, and the English title calls them best. ACS supports electron transfer from hair/clothing to balloons but does not establish cotton, wool and hair as the best or generally better than unspecified many other materials; charging also depends on the material pair and conditions. Hold the ungrounded comparative claim despite the clear static-electricity topic. Existing emphasis matches.

All three versions falsely infer nearby people are safe from Alert Level 0. PHIVOLCS explicitly says steam-driven/gas eruptions can occur without warning even at Taal Level 0, and danger-zone restrictions remain. Titles correctly name Level 0 but cannot offset the unsafe conclusion. No emphasis is specified; reject for volcano-alerts.

Pioneer weathering and soil formation could fit both proposed lessons, but BIS gudguron currently has only the candidate's surface-form attestation and needs lexical confirmation of the rock-breakdown mechanism. All versions also say other plants after discussing lichens, risking a plant-classification misconception. Titles and spans match; hold pending lexical/scientific clarification rather than treating the two category links as approval.

The English muscular-bag analogy is sound, but TL replaces stretchy with matatabang (fat/plump) and plural bags; BIS title Tinuod ingon Masel nga Sako does not identify the stomach at all. The BIS body retains muscular mixing, but full trilingual copy is not faithful. No emphasis is specified; hold digestion placement.

The English/TL threshing account is correct and could support agricultural separation products, but BIS linason and title Paggik need lexical/spelling confirmation. Corpus searching found no independent threshing attestation for these forms; the available dictionary endpoint did not resolve linas. Matching linason emphasis repeats the uncertainty. Hold both separation placements rather than approve unverified translated process names.

English, TL and BIS equate carbon in air with a gas called carbon dioxide without saying carbon is chemically combined with oxygen, and present that as the form of atmospheric carbon without qualification. This risks identifying the element itself as CO2 gas and ignores other carbon-containing atmospheric substances. Titles name CO2 correctly but bodies need precision before either states-of-matter or air-mixture use; no emphasis is specified.

Supersedes the original accept after a stronger lexical-authority check. Natural glass formation is sound and EN/TL/BIS bodies retain it, with matching emphasis. However, the BIS title Natural nga Baso changes the material to a drinking vessel: Wolff explicitly gives that vessel sense for basu, while the earlier Binisaya page expands senses of the English word glass automatically. That English sense expansion is not independent evidence for a Cebuano material sense. Hold g6:volcanic-materials pending title review.

The movable glottis adaptation is plausible, but never chokes is an unsupported absolute and BIS malumos can shift the claim toward drowning/suffocation. More decisively, this feeding adaptation addresses none of the proposed lesson's dry/flooded conditions, camouflage or mimicry foci. Titles and spans identify the breathing tube; they do not establish the required lesson fit.

Hand rubbing producing heat is correct in all three bodies and spans match. The TL/BIS titles instead use Alitan, whose technical meaning in Cebuano remains unresolved: the BIS corpus has only one independent body use equating it to friction, while the candidate body itself uses kiskisanay. Hold for lexical authority/native confirmation of the titles, not on a claim that a rare form is automatically ungrammatical.

The intact-sugar-molecule explanation is chemically sound, and TL/BIS faithfully preserve molecules, atoms and covalent bonds with matching spans. However, it adds secondary-school bonding terminology without explaining useful solutions, mixture properties or an application. For the proposed grade-6 useful-mixtures lesson, this is an unnecessarily advanced bonding digression rather than age-appropriate explicit supplemental coverage.

All three bodies label one long/short line pair as the battery symbol. Standard circuit notation distinguishes a cell's single pair from a battery's repeated pairs; the central diagram instruction collapses that distinction. Wire and lamp symbols, titles and matching spans are otherwise correct. Hold simple-circuits until the symbol instruction is precise.

TL/BIS faithfully preserve the 1.4-kg claim and emphasis, but the University of Michigan Animal Diversity Web account lists 1.05–1.2 kg; the proposed maximum was not confirmed. A mass fact alone also gives no investigation, measuring equipment or method. Hold the unverified number rather than use the investigation lesson as a repository for incidental measurements.

All three versions claim that movement of either source or observer changes wavelength. For sound, a moving observer encountering waves from a stationary source changes encounter frequency, not the wavelength in the medium; source movement is different. OpenStax distinguishes these cases. BIS also renders observed as nakit-an (seen), unhelpful for sound. Hold both wave-properties and moving-sound; titles reinforce the unconditional shorter/closer claim.

The three bodies agree, but the card aggregates Balatik, Moroporo and Mapulon under ancient Filipinos and asserts farmer/fisher seasonal use without identifying a community or source. National Museum evidence confirms Orion/Balatik and community-specific sky knowledge, but not this complete combined attribution. Hold both proposed lessons pending evidence for the named traditions; titles and no emphasis do not resolve that uncertainty.

All languages say the greater pull alone determines the winner. This neglects the essential force of ground friction and encourages a misleading account of the opposing rope forces. A university demonstration shows a wheeled-stool participant losing because floor friction is insufficient. Titles/spans retain the simplistic greater-force rule; hold contact-forces.

English/TL and the BIS body correctly define absence of a backbone, but the BIS title says Hayop nga Walang Bukog—animals with no bones—rather than no backbone, and includes Tagalog walang. That title changes the defining anatomical feature of the proposed animal-groups lesson. No emphasis is specified; hold full-copy approval.

The Crux navigation fact is accurate and both bodies preserve south-finding, with matching Southern Cross spans. However, the Tagalog title is copied as Krus sa Habagatan; the TL corpus has no body attestation for habagatan, while the TL body itself uses timog. Hold the unverified cross-language title pending lexical authority/native review, not because rarity alone proves a grammatical defect.

The elementary ideal-wave energy-transfer idea fits, but TL korotso for cork is unattested elsewhere in corpus bodies and unresolved by lookup. Both translations also start with Baon, whose carry-along question needs language confirmation. English's cork only bobbing vertically is itself an oversimplification of surface-water orbital motion. Hold the full copy; titles and no emphasis do not remedy these ambiguities.

Twice-yearly irrigated rice is plausible, but all languages present one fixed July–November/January–May calendar for the Philippines. IRRI documents different northern/southern production seasons and an Iloilo dry-season crop beginning October–November. The unlocalized months are unsuitable for a lesson explicitly including regional seasons. Titles and matched repetition spans are fine; hold the geographic overgeneralization.

The descriptions of familiar solids/liquids/gases and their mass are sound, and translations/spans faithfully match. However, Matter has three states is an unqualified exhaustive claim repeated in every language; plasma and other states exist. Hold both matter and states-of-matter until the scope is three common states, rather than teaching a false total.

Moon-driven tides would provide a useful remote-force example, but BIS uses nalubong (buried) for submerged; consulted dictionary material establishes bury/burial, not this underwater sense. The statements about reefs exposed at low tide also need an intertidal qualification. Titles and gravity spans match, but hold the current translation/scope ambiguity rather than generalize all reefs.

Rusting does form new substances, but every language falsely says the rust can never return to iron. Iron oxides can be reduced chemically; irreversibility is not the definition of a chemical change and this lesson explicitly guards that distinction. Titles and spans are consistent but reinforce an incorrect explanation.

The ordinary classroom observation that a small electromagnet strongly attracts iron is useful, but all versions categorically say electromagnets cannot pull aluminum and only iron-like metals respond. OpenStax classifies aluminum as paramagnetic, with weak attraction to applied fields. A strong-attraction/classroom-observation qualification is needed. Titles and iron spans match; hold the universal limit.

The amorphous volcanic-glass explanation is sound and all languages, titles and spans agree. The specific Taal occurrence was not verified: a consulted Philippine obsidian sourcing study identifies Nagcarlan and Pagudpod sources and does not establish Taal as a source. Hold both rock-observation and volcanic-materials rather than approve the unsupported local example.

English says it might not erupt; TL changes this into Hindi ito sasabog agad, a guarantee it will not erupt immediately. That contradicts the same card's sudden steam-blast warning and PHIVOLCS low-alert caution. BIS avoids this guarantee, but trilingual hazard copy must all be safe. Titles agree and no emphasis is specified; hold volcano-alerts.

English says stomach acid helps break down all the food you eat, which is overbroad: digestive acid primarily supports protein digestion and does not digest every food component, such as cellulose. TL/BIS omit all and otherwise convey acid aiding digestion correctly; titles and spans match. Hold the English universal claim in a lesson that distinguishes digestive-system functions.

Leucaena/ipil-ipil contour planting for erosion control is documented by FAO, so the English mechanism is plausible. BIS changes soil erosion to pagdahili sa yuta, a term independently used in the corpus for landslides/sliding; this needs confirmation before teaching the erosion versus mass-movement distinction. Titles preserve the broad protective theme and no spans are specified. Hold translation ambiguity rather than reject the agronomy.

The English names valid phase changes, but gives neither state properties, everyday examples nor the direction of any change, so the proposed states-of-matter lesson gets little explicit teaching beyond a list of terms. TL paghalumigmig and BIS pamuo also need authoritative condensation terminology confirmation; corpus repetitions alone do not settle those meanings. Titles and spans match; hold scope/lexical uncertainty.

The bodies correctly say removing forest can reduce local rain by removing transpiration. Both translated titles invert or muddle that relationship: Kagubatan na Bawas ng Ulan and Lasang nga Minus sa Ulan describe forest as reducing rain, unlike English Forests Feed the Rain. No emphasis is specified. Hold this title-level cause reversal for water-cycle.

Condensation contributes to visible whale breath, but English says the spout is just warm breath turning to mist. Whale blow can also contain expelled mucus and droplets; NOAA discusses sampled respiratory mucus. The exclusive claim is not established. TL/BIS preserve the simplified condensation account and spans match, but hold the full statement rather than treat all visible blow as pure condensation.

The Sun is plasma, but the specific over-99-percent-of-its-mass figure was not established. NASA's commonly quoted 99-percent figures concern the Sun's share of solar-system mass or plasma's share of visible cosmic matter, different denominators. All translations/titles repeat the unverified solar plasma percentage; TL also uses weight for mass. No emphasis is specified; hold numerical provenance.

Corm starch storage supporting taro regrowth is sound, and all languages, titles and spans preserve it. However, corms are a distinct specialized stem from this proposed lesson's named rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs and aerial roots. The card neither compares them nor identifies one of those structures. Hold the loose specialized-plant association rather than implicitly classify a corm as a bulb or tuber.

Ordinary rubber/plastic wire insulation is a valid conductor/insulator example and all bodies preserve the protective function. Both translated titles use unattested Blak, whose intended verb or noun is unclear; there are zero TL or BIS body attestations of that word. Hold title readability/lexical uncertainty for native review rather than asserting the insulating science is wrong.

The force-distance trade is correct for a force-multiplying ideal machine, but the body applies force reduction generically to a lever or pulley. A fixed pulley changes direction without reducing required force, and third-class levers can increase effort force. All translations/titles preserve the unqualified rule; spans match. Hold machine-investigation because the lesson includes advantages and limits that this wording erases.

The sungkit harvesting description is plausible and all titles, translations and spans retain it. However, a long reach alone is not an explanation of a simple machine: no fulcrum, lever action, wedge or force/distance mechanism is identified. Hold the proposed simple-machines placement rather than equating every useful tool with a taught machine class.

English correctly offers saltwater and air as separate homogeneous-mixture examples. TL tubig na may asin at hangin and BIS tubig nga adunay asin ug hangin can instead mean water containing salt and air, muddling which two solutions are being classified. Titles/spans are correct but the central example list needs disambiguation before useful-mixtures admission.

The approximate 78-percent nitrogen figure is correct, but every body says oxygen burns. Oxygen supports combustion; it is not the combustible fuel. This is a direct chemical misconception in the air-mixture lesson. Titles describe nitrogen and no spans are specified; hold regardless of the correct composition number.

A dugong exceeding 300 kg is plausible and TL/BIS faithfully preserve large size, slow swimming and mass; titles agree and no spans are specified. But a detached animal weight provides no investigation plan, equipment, measurement operation or comparison. Hold investigations scope; a numerical unit alone is not a useful investigation example.

The limestone-karst topic could support a local coastal landform, but the BIS title Pagbanlas Kemikal uses erosion/soil-washing wording for chemical weathering. Independent corpus pagbanlas examples are soil washed away, terracing and erosion; the body instead says in-place chemical weathering. TL title is also only generic chemical change. Hold this process distinction pending title review; spans themselves match.

All languages define an algal bloom using aquatic plants plus algae, then imply eventual oxygen loss and fish death as inevitable. NOAA distinguishes harmless blooms from harmful ones and notes oxygen depletion as one possible impact. The title reinforces danger without that distinction; spans match. Hold the overgeneralized ecosystem-effect claim.

The sexual/asexual comparison is false as a general plant rule: sexual reproduction also occurs in nonflowering plants, and self-fertilization need not involve two parent plants. Asexual seed formation also exists. All three bodies repeat the flowers/seeds/two-parents requirement, with consistent titles/spans. Hold plant-reproduction; the copied distinction would teach central misconceptions.

English/TL correctly describe approaching compression and receding stretching for a moving source. BIS changes stretch to moguba, meaning break/destroy, so it says the waves break as the ambulance leaves. Dictionary confirms the guba root. Titles and Doppler-effect spans match but the central receding-wave explanation is mistranslated.

The intended repeated-trial control is sensible, but always use the same drop height is unqualified even though height may itself be the intended independent variable. TL ibabawang bagay does not clearly convey dropping, and BIS itulo lacks independent body attestation for releasing a solid object. Titles are about drop height and no spans are specified; hold the unclear experiment context and action wording.

The backward-water/forward-boat relationship is an action-reaction example, but the proposed lesson concerns an object's motion in the same direction as the force applied to it. The card never identifies the water's forward force on the boat, so it superficially presents opposite directions without the necessary two-body distinction. TL/BIS preserve that omission; titles and backward spans match. Hold exact lesson fit.

The definition and examples are correct across languages and titles/spans match. However, more than nine out of ten animals uses an unspecified counting unit; the AMNH figure is explicitly about animal species, not individual animals on Earth. The card needs the same denominator rather than turning species diversity into a population statistic. Hold the numerical claim.

Air having weight in Earth's gravity is correct and all three bodies retain it. However, the only proposed lesson is explicitly mass and occupied space; neither property is stated, and weight must not silently be substituted for mass. Titles agree and no spans are specified. Hold the placement until there is an explicit conceptual link rather than an incidental related property.

The cylinder/displacement choices are reasonable, but regular solids use multiplied dimensions is not a general volume rule for all regular shapes; different shapes need specific formulas. TL/BIS further reduce this to increasing/multiplying sukat without identifying which dimensions or operation. Titles and volume spans agree, but the mathematical instruction is too vague to admit as measuring-volume guidance.

Both named eruption years are real, but the claimed decades-long rest is inferred from a selectively paired 1965 and 2020 record. PHIVOLCS/JICA histories include intervening eruptions through 1977; the copy obscures the actual quiet interval and models bad historical inference. TL/BIS and titles reproduce the same misleading chronology; no spans are specified. Hold eruption-history.

English describes an apparently frozen pattern while water still moves. TL humihinto ng galaw and BIS mopahunong sa lihok instead say the flashing light stops the wave's motion, omitting that it only appears stationary. The final moving-water clause leaves an unresolved contradiction. Titles and no spans do not fix this stroboscopic-mechanism mistranslation; hold water-waves.

Unpowered gliding descends relative to still air, but always goes downward is false for ground-relative motion in rising air. Every translation repeats the unqualified downward rule; TL/BIS also use floating terminology that does not by itself distinguish gliding. Titles are generic flight and spans match. Hold gravity until the still-air/frame condition is clear.

The EN/TL diagram instruction correctly locates the paired ovaries beside the uterus. BIS repeats unresolved porma-ovo for oval shape and uses gihulma (formed/shaped) for drawn. The only corpus porma-ovo examples are the same generated ovary family, so independent lexical support remains absent. Titles fit and no spans are specified; hold consistently with the related ovary card.

The at-home build invitation omits insulated wire, battery limits and prompt disconnection. Thin bare wire around an iron nail directly across a battery can short and heat; identical omissions persist in TL/BIS. Titles and electromagnet spans agree but do not make the procedure suitable for unsupervised children. Hold construction/observations until the core safety conditions are stated.

English retains likely, but TL/BIS turn hazardous eruption probability into an unqualified eruption within hours/days; TL title Likas is also ambiguous compared with evacuate. PHIVOLCS Level 4 interpretations depend on the volcano and can include ongoing eruptive activity. Evacuating designated danger zones is correct, but the generic certainty/timing rule is not. Titles and no spans do not resolve it; hold volcano-alerts.

English describes weathering rock, but TL ginugupit means cutting/snipping the rock surface rather than wearing it down. BIS scraping wording also needs care, and other plants risks treating lichens as plants. Titles and no emphasis do not repair the mechanism/classification issue. Hold soil-formation; a clearer lichen candidate has been accepted separately.

The English and Tagalog give useful variation, inheritance and reproductive-success conditions, and all emphasis spans match. Cebuano substitutes nagpanamkon og daghan for reproducing more: Binisaya identifies panamkon with pregnancy cravings and its root with conceiving. That does not reliably express differential reproduction across organisms. Hold both evolution placements pending lexical correction/review; titles themselves are aligned.

The English elastic-storage/rebound example could support both proposed lessons, but current translations leave the physical comparison uncertain: Tagalog namumukol does not unambiguously convey compression, and Cebuano lapok names mud where English specifies clay. Binisaya supports the mud sense (with a broad clay gloss), so this is a contextual uncertainty, not a global ban on lapok. The clipped phrase titles add no clarification. Hold for precise trilingual material/deformation wording; no emphasis is present.

The titles and matching momentum emphasis align in all languages, but every body says total momentum stays the same in a collision without defining an isolated system or negligible external impulse. This unconditional statement can mislead when external forces act. OpenStax explicitly requires zero net external force; hold the conservation lesson until that condition is present.

The English describes DNA-informed rice breeding, but Tagalog bigas and Cebuano bugas in the drought-survival clause can describe harvested/milled grains rather than living rice plants (the titles correctly use palay/humay). Binisaya explicitly lists milled rice/food grain for bugas. Hold this material referent ambiguity. Independently, g10:l-8 is not established: studying DNA for breeding does not explicitly identify genetic engineering, GMOs or IVF. DNA emphasis matches in all languages.

The endangered-turtle topic and matching organism emphasis are aligned across languages, but the card only says most endangered, not the explicit Critically Endangered classification needed by g9:l-6. The IUCN specialist account gives that category and describes adults as semi-aquatic in lowland forests; lives only in freshwater is too exclusive. Hold for both conservation-category precision and habitat scope rather than infer the missing classification.

English, Tagalog and Cebuano consistently offer only a few cm/year and a fingernail analogy, with no direction, reference frame or measured trench segment. A consulted USGS regional account reports roughly 10 cm/year plate convergence partitioned over multiple boundaries, which does not validate this particular trench rate. Hold the quantitative claim and proposed future-position lesson; the body cannot support a defensible archipelago projection. Titles are topic-aligned and no emphasis is present.

Titles and convection emphasis are aligned across all three languages, but each body characterizes mantle rock generally as almost melted and presents a simple upward/downward push as the plate-driving mechanism. USGS distinguishes solid mantle that flows over long times from small localized melt regions. Hold the material-state ambiguity before using it to explain plate-driving mechanisms; the card also omits the asthenosphere, slab pull and ridge push.

Current bodies discuss opposite momentum changes, not the equal opposite forces required by the only proposed lesson g9:f-4. That relationship is inferable but unstated, so the placement is too loose. English additionally claims total momentum is exactly unchanged without defining the rocket-plus-exhaust system or external-force condition; TL/BIS omit that conservation clause. Titles and emphasis match the momentum topic. Hold rather than import the missing force explanation.

All three bodies explicitly define tectonic plates as pieces of crust, omitting their rigid uppermost-mantle component. That is a consequential definition error in a plate-tectonics lesson. Titles and uplift outcome otherwise align, but the generic collision statement cannot justify carrying that inaccurate plate definition into g10:e-7. No emphasis is present.

Every language tells the child to switch off the main power first during an electrical fire, without an if-safe condition, adult help or evacuation priority. The no-water warning is useful, and titles/emphasis match, but the imperative can send a child toward hazardous equipment. USFA child guidance prioritizes leaving and staying out. Hold both safety placements until the current instruction is safe.

Titles and all three bodies consistently state force times duration, but omit that impulse uses constant force or the average net force when force varies. The word exactly makes this an unconditional formula claim. OpenStax states the constant-force assumption explicitly; hold the standalone definition until its condition is included. No emphasis is present.

The three bodies say growth stays fast until the population hits the limit and only then slows. Logistic growth instead slows while approaching carrying capacity as resources become limiting. That timing is the precise learning point of g10:l-11, so this is not merely omitted detail. Titles and population emphasis align, but the science requires correction.

The English heat-to-steam electricity concept is potentially useful, but Tagalog binabarena tayo and Cebuano ginabarena ta make us the entity being drilled rather than clearly expressing that people drill. Corpus search finds only this card for both constructions. Hold the actor ambiguity and blanket safely assurance; no device chain is explained. The proposed g10:f-13 placement is also weak because the text supplies no renewable/nonrenewable comparison or environmental impact. Titles and emphasis are otherwise aligned.

Each body makes the same unqualified same-group/same-outer-electron-count assertion. Helium has two valence electrons while other group-18 elements have eight, and transition groups need further care. The proposed lesson explicitly includes exceptions, so this standalone rule is misleading without a main-group qualification and helium exception. Titles are aligned and no emphasis is present.

English/TL and the opening Cebuano clause correctly distinguish beneficial, harmful and neutral outcomes. The final Cebuano walay bali is uncertain in this neutrality sense: the corpus has only this body for that phrase and other bali uses concern breaks/bending; the attempted dictionary lookup yielded no accessible definition. This is a lexical hold, not a proven global false-friend claim. Titles are aligned and no emphasis exists; do not admit until that current phrase is resolved.

Every body says predators keep prey close to carrying capacity. Predation can regulate prey well below the resource-limited carrying capacity, so that near-capacity outcome is not a general consequence. Titles and carrying-capacity emphasis are aligned, but this misleading ecology rule should not support g10:l-10; the card also does not specify food, water, shelter or mates as limiting resources.

The three bodies incorrectly explain any nonzero net force as one force being stronger than the others. Equal forces in different non-opposite directions can have a nonzero vector sum. This is a definition error, not just a missing example. Titles and unbalanced-forces emphasis match, but hold the net-force lesson until the scalar stronger-force shortcut is removed.

All three bodies make a strong undersea earthquake sufficient to create a tsunami while omitting sudden water displacement. NOAA explicitly says not all earthquakes cause tsunamis and identifies seafloor displacement as the mechanism. This is the proposed lesson's central distinction, so the force/energy-only explanation is inadequate and potentially misleading. Titles are aligned; no emphasis exists.

The work formula is unconditional force times distance in all languages; it omits the component of force along displacement and cannot handle perpendicular forces or negative work. The proposed lesson explicitly includes direction. Titles and work emphasis align, but the central formula needs its parallel-force condition before use.

The annual debris-crossing mechanism is broadly correct, but every language attributes both Perseids and Geminids to comet dust. NASA identifies the Geminids' parent as asteroid 3200 Phaethon. Titles and emphasis are aligned; hold the false named example instead of relying on its otherwise useful annual timing.

The English/TL/BIS bodies all say chloroplasts occur only in plant cells. Photosynthetic protists also have chloroplasts, as OpenStax explicitly describes; only is therefore false in the unqualified current claim. The sunlight/photosynthesis role, titles and matching emphasis are otherwise aligned. Hold rather than teach an incorrect exclusivity rule.

The Atlantic seafloor-spreading example is useful, but all languages open with a general statement that our oceans are growing; ocean basins do not all widen. The title also shifts the growth to the ridges rather than clearly the spreading basin. Hold this scope ambiguity. g8:plates-crust additionally lacks a link from crust to lithospheric plate composition; g10:e-2 has a plausible divergent-boundary example but it does not override the current wording problem. No emphasis is present.

The simplified different-sized-atom account can explain strengthening in some alloys, but every body generalizes that an alloy becomes harder to bend or break; hardness, strength and brittleness are not interchangeable across alloys. More decisively for g9:m-10, the card supplies neither the sea-of-electrons bonding model nor electrical/thermal conduction. Titles are aligned and no emphasis exists. Hold rather than use a loose all-metals association.

The cubic sodium-chloride lattice is correct, but each body promises that every visible salt grain is a cube. Ground, fractured or differently grown salt crystals need not be perfect cubes; the proposed microscope observation can directly contradict the claim. Titles and CUBE emphasis amplify this overstatement. Hold until crystal structure is distinguished from every grain's external shape.

All three bodies generalize to cave animals and give energy saving as the definitive cause of eye reduction. Research on cavefish discusses multiple genetic/selection mechanisms and population differences, so this needs a qualified organism-specific account rather than purposeful eyes-shrank-to-save-energy wording. TL/BIS also move from tiny eyes to eyes disappearing. The titles do not resolve the overgeneralization; no emphasis exists.

All bodies promise exactly salt and water whenever any acid meets any base. That requires qualification to the intended hydroxide-neutralization cases; bases such as ammonia can form a salt with acid without producing water. Titles and emphasized word equation preserve the same overgeneralization. Hold before using this as a general word-equation recipe in g10:m-5.

The moles-per-litre-of-solution definition is scientifically correct and all titles/emphasis align, but the proposed Grade 7 lesson measures solute against a stated solvent volume. Solution volume is a different denominator, and the card introduces moles without its prerequisite. Hold this exact placement rather than substitute an advanced concentration metric for the supplied lesson target.

The approximate six-month polar day/night and tilt explanation is suitable science at the poles, and titles/emphasis align. However, the Cebuano sequence uses unay where English says then. The corpus has no independent temporal use; Binisaya defines unay with accessible/attached/mainland/self-inflict senses, not the required transition. Hold this unresolved current-copy error rather than silently reading a corrected conjunction.

All three bodies and titles accurately identify FaultFinder's intended active-fault proximity function, and emphasis matches. Current PHIVOLCS evidence, however, says FaultFinder is unavailable for security work and directs users to HazardHunterPH. Its capability page also describes mapped proximity, not the English promise of an exact house/school fault distance. Hold current availability/precision until copy is reconciled with the official service state.

All three bodies change no fixed shape into water with no shape at all. Liquids have a shape set by their container; the state change removes a fixed shape rather than shape itself. The particle loosening language and titles reinforce an incomplete account without energy transfer. Hold the central state-property error; no emphasis exists.

The three bodies restrict the definition of fragmentation to two parts, though fragmentation can yield more than two. The capability/large-enough qualifications are useful and the title/emphasis match, but the definition needs correction before the example supports asexual reproduction. It also does not explicitly discuss offspring genetic similarity; no procedure should be inferred from the body.

All languages correctly qualify ten percent as approximate, but then assign all remaining energy to activity/respiration/heat. Energy also remains in uneaten or unassimilated biomass and enters detrital pathways. Hold this overly exhaustive remainder account. g7:trophic-levels also has no producer/consumer/pyramid identification; g7:energy-transfer is a clear intended fit once the energy accounting is sound. Titles align and no emphasis exists.

The current question and answers describe rapidly moving electrons arranged in surrounding layers without saying this is a shell/energy-level model rather than a physical electron path. TL umiikot and BIS naglibot strengthen the orbit reading. The proposed lesson explicitly guards against exact shell paths. Titles and emphasis match, but hold until the model limitation is explicit enough not to teach a miniature planetary trajectory.

The body's stratospheric ozone/UV-protection account is sound in all three languages and emphasis matches. Tagalog title Sapot ng Osono, however, uses the web sense where the English and Cebuano name a layer. Corpus review found 23 Tagalog body uses of sapot, with the inspected contexts consistently spider-web material, not atmospheric layer. Hold this title-sense uncertainty rather than promote a misleading title on a radiation lesson.

UV exposure, DNA damage and later skin-cancer risk are real, but English title Sunburn Is UV DNA Damage and all bodies identify DNA damage as the direct acute sunburn mechanism. The 2024 Molecular Cell study and its 2025 university report identify RNA-damage/ribotoxic response as the acute driver. Hold this mechanistic oversimplification; the cancer-risk warning remains valid. TL/BIS preserve the same causal claim; no emphasis exists.

The electron-sharing water example and matching body emphasis are scientifically suitable, but TL/BIS title Kobalenteng Bono has unresolved bond terminology. The corpus has four chemical-body uses in Tagalog but zero in Cebuano; the attempted Cebuano dictionary lookup did not supply a definition. Since the corpus itself can propagate generator errors, hold the unsupported Cebuano title sense pending lexical review, without claiming all uses of bono are wrong.

The typical large plant central vacuole/smaller animal vacuole contrast is useful, but all bodies turn it into a universal just-one-permanent versus many-temporary rule. FSU describes many plant cells and animal vacuoles tending to be smaller, appropriately qualifying these variable organelles. Titles and emphasis match. Hold the unqualified cell-type rule until typical cells are distinguished from all cells.

Each body makes horizontal speed constant for projectile motion without the necessary negligible-air-resistance/other-horizontal-force assumption. It also labels the vertical component downward even during an upward launch. Titles and projectile emphasis match, but the unconditional rule is unsuitable for the everyday-projectile investigation lesson until the ideal model is stated.

The three bodies correctly recommend turning off unused electrical loads and give cost/environment benefits. Tagalog title Pag-iipon ng Kuryente, however, can describe accumulating/storing electricity rather than reducing use. Both independent corpus body uses of pag-iipon concern accumulating rainwater or dirty water. Hold this unresolved title sense; Cebuano pagtipig is not flagged, since its saving sense is attested. No emphasis exists.

All three bodies faithfully describe a familiar baking-soda/vinegar toy and matching chemical emphasis, but the proposed scientific-model lesson targets explaining unseen phenomena and model limitations. This card only says the toy looks like an eruption and supplies no real-volcano relationship or limit; its chemistry is not the volcanic process. Hold the loose model-label placement rather than credit unseen-process understanding.

The current claim is about dissolution speed, consistently translated with matching faster-dissolving emphasis. The proposed lesson concerns solubility/saturation, the amount that can dissolve at equilibrium. Faster is not more soluble, so admitting this card would blur the exact distinction under study. Titles are aligned; hold placement rather than treat the shared temperature keyword as sufficient.

The three bodies state that noble gases are completely unreactive. Xenon and other heavier noble gases can form compounds, so a full valence shell explains low usual reactivity rather than absolute impossibility. Titles align but intensify the full-shell rule; no emphasis exists. Hold all three placements rather than teaching the incorrect absolute.

All three languages attach the two-allele rule to most traits rather than to a diploid autosomal gene/locus. Many human traits are polygenic, so most traits do not correspond to just two inherited alleles. The one-from-each-parent idea would fit g7:inherited-information after that qualification; g8:inheritance-patterns also has no dominant/recessive or multigeneration pattern. Titles share the same oversimplification and no emphasis exists.

All three bodies explicitly claim copper atoms are not chemically bonded. Metallic bonding is what holds the copper solid together; copper is an element because it contains one atomic/proton-number type, not because bonding is absent. Titles and element emphasis match, but the causal explanation is false and must not enter g8:pure-substances.

TL pagpapalala and BIS pagpalala replace fermenting with a worsening sense; the Cebuano corpus uses the root in worsening floods/erosion, and no independent fermentation sense was found. The Cebuano title also has an unresolved Ilang phrase instead of rice wine. DOST identifies the tapuy starter as bubod/binukbok, so the asserted tapay name needs local sourcing. Hold science/translation identity before considering the fermentation placement; no emphasis exists.

All three bodies and emphasis preserve the proposed mouth-color reaction, but the card presents chewing areca/betel nut with lime as a child-facing chemistry curiosity without any hazard context. IARC identifies areca/betel-quid chewing as carcinogenic. Hold age suitability of this standalone oral-exposure example and the insufficiently identified color-reaction claim; do not treat its mention of color as enough for g10:m-1.

Full/new-moon spring-tide flooding is a useful example, but all languages imply that other days are neap tides. Neap tides occur around the quarter phases, with intermediate tidal ranges between those extrema. The binary schedule is too loose for g8:tide-motions; titles and spring-tide emphasis otherwise match. Hold the phase/range account.

All three bodies call a decreasing distance-time trace a return toward the start. Accumulated distance cannot decrease; this would require a position/displacement or explicitly distance-from-origin axis. Even distance from origin alone cannot identify a unique direction. The proposed lesson specifically warns that the graph alone does not show direction. Titles/emphasis match the mistaken rule; hold.

The continental-origin statement is broadly relevant geology, but every language attributes modern Palawan–Borneo animal resemblance directly to Palawan drifting from Asia. Primary vertebrate research instead examines later Pleistocene land-bridge/colonization history; the card supplies no fossil, rock or tectonic chronology to establish that causal shortcut. Hold both the causal claim and loose continental-drift evidence placement. Titles align and no emphasis exists.

English qualifies strongest shaking with usually, but Tagalog and Cebuano remove that qualification and assert maximum shaking at the epicenter. Local ground conditions, rupture geometry and distance can move the strongest shaking elsewhere. The epicenter is specifically above the focus, not defined by shaking strength. Titles align; no emphasis exists. Hold the cross-language certainty increase in this earthquake lesson.

The floating-equilibrium physics in English/TL is correct, but Cebuano substitutes gitudlo nga tubig for displaced water. Binisaya gives tudlo as point/indicate/teach rather than displacement. That changes the essential quantity in Archimedes' condition. Titles and weight emphasis match, but hold the current Cebuano body before using the balanced-force example.

English presents higher risk of water/crop impacts, and Cebuano retains peligro, but Tagalog changes that into asserted water shortage and crop damage. PAGASA uses likelihood and regional differences for El Niño rainfall impacts. Hold the certainty increase and unqualified national dry-spell wording; titles are aligned and no emphasis exists.

The conductor/insulator contrast is useful, but every body concludes that touching the wire will not shock the child simply because of its plastic coating. Insulation must be intact and suitable; damaged cables or live conductors remain hazardous. TL/BIS make the no-shock assurance particularly categorical. Titles and no-emphasis formatting are aligned, but hold both safety placements until the guarantee is qualified.

The English/BIS extra-CO₂ heat-retention account fits enhanced greenhouse warming, and titles identify trapping heat. Tagalog uses natatabunan ang init, which the corpus otherwise supports as covered/buried material rather than retained outgoing heat. The body does not clarify that metaphor. Hold this unresolved translation of the central mechanism rather than silently substituting the title's nagkukulong sense. No emphasis exists.

The three bodies give generic gloves as a barrier against heat, cuts or chemicals without explaining that different glove materials are selected for different hazards. That omission is consequential in a handling-safety lesson: ordinary laboratory gloves do not safely cover all those hazards. OSHA explicitly ties glove performance to the anticipated hazard. Titles and glove emphasis match; hold until suitable-glove selection is part of the advice.

EN correctly describes radio as electromagnetic radiation, distinct from sound and able to propagate in vacuum; TL preserves that explanation, and the titles and emphasis are aligned. BIS uses makalakaw for propagation through space. Binisaya directly glosses lakaw as walking; the travel entries on that page are broader English semantic relations, not direct attestation of this Cebuano wave-propagation usage. Hold this uncertain lexical choice for native or stronger lexical review, rather than asserting that every figurative use is wrong. The vacuum focus would fit g9:f-10 once the current BIS wording is resolved.

The current text confuses the broad base of an energy pyramid with a necessarily large number of individual plants: an energy pyramid represents available energy, while organism-number pyramids can have one tree supporting many consumers. Its additional claim that plants supply the starting energy for every other living thing excludes non-plant producers and chemosynthetic food webs. TL and BIS preserve the overgeneralization; their Pyamide titles also contain a spelling defect. Neither g7:trophic-levels nor g7:energy-transfer should receive this current card.

All three bodies state an unconditional rule that adding heat makes atoms/molecules vibrate faster and increases their spacing. Added heat during a phase change need not raise temperature, and expansion is not universal for every material and temperature range. Calling all particle motion vibration also leaves the state of matter unspecified. The aligned titles and heat emphasis do not qualify these claims. Hold for g7:particle-motion because the present statement would teach an overgeneralized heat-temperature-spacing relationship.

EN/TL/BIS consistently describe fin removal and population harm, and their titles/emphasis are aligned; the non-graphic conservation topic is age appropriate. The added claim that coral reefs depend on sharks and are therefore harmed as a general consequence is too categorical across shark species and reef contexts. Global reef surveys support fishing-related shark depletion, while primary work on mesopredators describes context-dependent ecological effects. Hold the whole current card rather than approve only its first clause. The threat example would fit g9:l-7, but g9:l-10 also lacks its specific deforestation/pollution/invasive or evidence-evaluation focus.

All three bodies and their emphasized 38-ATP spans repeat a single unqualified aerobic-respiration yield. That is an older idealized estimate based on particular assumptions, not a reliable general yield for glucose respiration across cells. Contemporary quantitative work and plant bioenergetic analysis show that coupling, transport, and alternative pathways affect ATP yield. ATP molecules also carry usable chemical energy rather than being molecules of energy themselves. Hold g8:photosynthesis-respiration despite the otherwise correct glucose/oxygen and carbon-dioxide/water participants; do not replace one universal number with another.

The EN and TL bodies give a plausible broad shell-internalization account and correctly compare an ancestral shell with, rather than descend modern cuttlefish from, a nautilus. BIS retains cuttlefish in the body but titles the card Bukog sa Nukos. The consulted dictionary directly glosses nukos as squid; a cuttlefish-specific usage is not established there, and a squid pen is not a cuttlebone. Hold this organism-name uncertainty for native or stronger lexical evidence, rather than trusting a perceived umbrella meaning. The morphology example could support g10:l-5 after resolution. Cuttlebone emphasis is present in every body.

The solar/wind comparison is relevant to g10:e-12, but EN, TL, and BIS all turn low operational emissions into an unqualified claim that this electricity adds no greenhouse gases. The lifecycle assessment dataset separates upstream, operating, and downstream emissions and does not support zero total emissions. The card supplies no operational boundary that would make its absolute wording reliable. The BIS title Solar Wind Gas also drops the reduced/no-emissions relation in the other titles. Hold the current trilingual card; Philippine sunshine alone does not establish a universally perfect generation resource.

The EN body correctly places replacement-cell mitosis in deeper skin layers; BIS preserves deeper layers and the mitosis title. TL instead says mitosis occurs sa ilalim ng balat, under the skin, changing the anatomical location. The consulted dictionary supports the under/beneath reading, while epidermal-renewal sources place the relevant dividing cells within the epidermis, principally its basal layer. Titles alone do not resolve that body mismatch. Hold g7:cell-division until the TL location is accurate; skin renewal itself is an appropriate and useful growth/repair example.

The yearly axial-direction explanation is scientifically acceptable: NASA describes the tilted axis maintaining approximately the same direction during an orbit, with the north axis near Polaris. EN/TL titles and bodies convey that idea, and all tilt emphasis spans match. BIS uses nagaturo for points. A full local root check found ten pointing-context bodies, but these machine-translated repetitions do not establish lexical correctness; Binisaya directly attests tudlo for pointing, while Wolff supplies different meanings for turu. Hold the unresolved Cebuano lexical choice for native or stronger independent evidence, rather than declare a new universal false-friend rule. g7:sunlight-angle would otherwise fit the tilt/orbit focus.

All three bodies and titles preserve the instruction to add two or more batteries in series and the promised much-brighter bulb. Voltages add for correctly oriented sources, but the present instruction gives neither compatible battery/bulb ratings nor a bound on added voltage; a bulb can be overdriven and burn out rather than reliably shine brighter. A primary engineering classroom source confirms excessive filament current can destroy the bulb. The unbounded imperative is unsuitable as a standalone child circuit instruction. Hold g9:f-7 despite the useful underlying series-voltage relationship; no copy repair or substituted activity is authorized.
